title: Geneva International Discussions on Georgia open under OSCE, UN and EU chairmanship
body:
On 15 October 2008 the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), the United Nations and the European Union co-chaired discussions on Georgia in Geneva. The meeting followed the Six Point Agreement of 12 August 2008 and the 8 September implementing arrangements. It was the first round of what became known as the Geneva International Discussions.

According to the OSCE press release, the afternoon session was adjourned, and the parties agreed to meet again, with the next session set for 18 November 2008. OSCE Special Envoy Heikki Talvitie said the process had begun and that all participants showed a readiness to engage, adding: "Our aim is very practical; to strengthen stability in the region and improve the humanitarian situation."

The format brings together representatives of Georgia, Russia, the United States and of Abkhazia and South Ossetia. Discussions are organised in two working groups, one on security and stability and one on the return of displaced persons and refugees. Reports of the opening day varied: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported that the talks stumbled over procedural disagreements, and Georgia blamed Russia for obstructing the working groups. The meetings have continued in Geneva in repeated rounds since then.
